GECKO GOLF - a RetroStone VC game for Windows
(c) 2026 Pierre-Louis Boyer (8BCraft). Code MIT, art/music/sound CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: see LICENSE-geckogolf.txt.

A little leopard gecko plays golf on a course that never ends: one hole after
another over rolling meadows, desert dunes, snowy hills, a night course and a
candy land, each hole starting where the last ball dropped in. Aim, hold to
charge the swing, let go. Mind the sand that stops the ball, the ice that
slides, the bouncy mushrooms and the water (a penalty stroke). You start with
12 strokes; each shot spends one, a hole in one gives 3 back and a hole in two
2. Your score is the holes you complete before the strokes run out. Medals at
6, 12, 24 and 40 holes, and your best is kept.

Run GeckoGolf.exe. No installation needed (SDL2 is built in).

Controls                  Gamepad (SNES layout)      Keyboard
  aim                       D-pad (held: faster)       arrow keys
                            Up / Down: higher / lower, Left / Right: turn
  charge, shoot             hold A, let go             hold X, let go
  no shot (while charging)  B                          Z
  start                     A (or Start, D-pad)        X or Enter
  pause / resume            Select (or Start in a run) Backspace or Esc
  players 2-4 join          A on their pad, on the title (B leaves)
  back to the title         A (or Select) on the results
  touch / mouse             a slingshot: put a finger down, pull back away
                            from where the ball should go (the farther, the
                            harder), let go to shoot; a tap starts

Up to four geckos (orange, blue, green and purple) play the same holes, each
with their own ball, pad and strokes: the one farthest from the cup plays
next. A player is out when their strokes run out; the results rank everyone by
holes, then by the fewest strokes, with medals.

F11 or Alt+Enter: fullscreen. F12: screenshot. Close the window to quit.
Options: GeckoGolf.exe --scale 4 --fullscreen
The best score is saved in geckogolf.srm next to the exe.
